Welcome. These four workbooks are the primary documents you'll use during the Blockseminar. Each day has its own workbook — a Quarto document you read, follow, and type alongside on your own laptop.

The workbooks are a **companion** to the course book (linked at the top right). The book goes deeper on every topic; the workbooks keep you moving through the workshop with just enough explanation to understand what you're doing and why.

## The four days

| Day   | Date         | Workbook                 | Focus                                            |
|-------|--------------|--------------------------|--------------------------------------------------|
| Day 1 | Fri 18 Dec   | [Day 1](day1.qmd)        | Foundations — RStudio, Git, data, `dplyr`, `ggplot2` |
| Day 2 | Sat 19 Dec   | [Day 2](day2.qmd)        | Text analytics                                    |
| Day 3 | Fri 8 Jan    | [Day 3](day3.qmd)        | Statistics and modelling                          |
| Day 4 | Sat 9 Jan    | [Day 4](day4.qmd)        | Reproducible publishing                           |

## How the workbooks work

Each workbook has:

- **A short intro** — what today is about and what you'll have built by the end
- **Numbered sections** (§1, §2, …) — each with a narrative walkthrough and executable code
- **Exercises at the end of each section** — starter code with gaps for you to fill in
- **A solutions section at the end** — complete worked solutions, numbered to match the exercises

The exercises are marked `eval: false` so the workbook renders cleanly even if you haven't filled in the gaps yet. When you complete an exercise, change the chunk option to `eval: true` and re-render to see your output.

## Rendering the workbook

To render a workbook yourself:

1. Make sure you have the required packages installed (see each day's setup section)
2. Make sure the required data files are in your project's `data/` folder
3. Open the `.qmd` file in RStudio
4. Click the **Render** button at the top of the editor

The rendered HTML sits next to the source file. You can open it in a browser, or just use RStudio's preview pane.

- **During the Blockseminar:** raise your hand

- **Where to look first:** the relevant chapter in the course book, then Stack Overflow

Good luck. You've got this.
